headline: Derivatives swing and weak gas prices flip results to a loss
summary_short: Matador's Q1 2026 revenue fell 33.8% y/y to $672M as a collapse in realized natural gas prices and a $255.5M unrealized derivatives loss swung the company to a $35.9M net loss (-$0.29 diluted EPS), versus $240.1M net income a year ago.
summary_long: Oil production and price both rose y/y, but a natural gas price collapse (-82% to $0.64/Mcf) cut gas revenue 81%. A $255.5M unrealized derivatives loss (vs a $5.1M gain last year) and a $15.6M loss on debt extinguishment from redeeming the 2028 Notes drove the swing from $240.1M net income to a $35.9M net loss (-$0.29 diluted EPS). Management's own Adjusted EBITDA fell 10% y/y to $577.2M on the weaker gas price, partly offset by higher production. Cash rose to $30.5M after a $737.9M 2034 Notes offering funded the 2028 Notes redemption. FY2026 capex guidance: $1.35-$1.44B D/C/E plus $100-110M midstream capex.

drivers.explanation: Oil revenue rose 5% on higher production and a slightly higher realized price, but natural gas revenue fell 81% as the realized gas price collapsed 82% y/y, and total revenue also absorbed a $255.5M unrealized derivatives loss versus a $5.1M gain a year ago.

Total expenses were roughly flat while revenue fell; DD&A rose 4% on higher production and G&A rose 16% on higher stock-based compensation, partly offset by lower purchased-natural-gas and other-tax costs.

Tracks operating income's decline, plus the $255.5M unrealized derivatives loss and a $15.6M loss on debt extinguishment from redeeming the 2028 Notes; partly offset by an $83.6M lower income-tax provision tied to the OBBBA.
Follows net income's swing to a loss; diluted weighted-average shares were little changed (123.5M vs 125.3M a year ago).

Not explained in the release as a discrete plain-EBITDA line — Matador discloses Adjusted EBITDA instead, which fell 10% y/y to $577.2M on lower realized gas prices, partly offset by higher oil and gas production.
Cash rose as $737.9M of net proceeds from the new 2034 Notes offering, plus a sale-leaseback financing, more than covered the 2028 Notes tender/redemption per the financing-activities discussion.
Capital expenditures fell year-over-year on lower midstream capex and lower land/seismic acquisition spend, per the investing-activities discussion.

Management frames the quarter around a $255.5M unrealized derivatives loss that flipped GAAP results to a loss, even as Adjusted EBITDA of $577.2M reflects continued production growth (+5% oil, +4% gas) against a sharp drop in realized natural gas prices.
